comments.body:
Evidence basis for this plan (read-only investigation, 2026-08-29, no LLM calls):

Corpus (fresh origin/tickets): 5,985 tickets; 1,283 with ≥1 plan-review sidecar; 4,317 sidecars in tree (14 v1, 4,303 v2), PASS 2,329 / BLOCK 1,821 / INDETERMINATE 167, 2026-06-27→08-29; impact cohorts plan-v5 2,117 / v4 1,520 / v3 662 / v2 16; ~4,988 REVIEW_RESULT files pruned from the tree, ~40% plan-review by sample, all recoverable from git history. LMN store: 515 tickets, 31 with reviews, 74 sidecars (all v2, plan-v5, Bedrock Sonnet). 946 tickets with ≥2 reviews; 2,483 consecutive changed-material pairs (BLOCK→PASS 788, BLOCK→BLOCK 847, PASS→PASS 569); 551 identical-material pairs of which 208 flipped verdict. Labels: plan_defect bug closes 84, caused_by links 89, plan-PASS→completion-FAIL 199 tickets, reopens 18 (of 21) on reviewed tickets. Plan text reconstruction: 3,768 of 4,317 reviews predate their ticket's latest SNAPSHOT, so EDIT replay from git history is required; the stored material_fingerprint (material_diff.material_basis) verifies the reconstruction exactly.

Pipeline seams: Pass 3 is deterministic (review_kernel/decide.py) and fully replayable from sidecar findings[].verification + block_threshold + blocking_enabled (proven by docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py). Pass 2 is a pure function with injectable run_chunk (review_kernel/verify.py); the verifier eval spec lacks a run_case arm. Pass 1 needs live Opus. Sidecars do not persist prompts, raw responses, pass-2 analysis text or pass-1 affirmations.

Cost (from .rebar/usage.jsonl, 11,902 rows, priced with genai-prices Bedrock ids: Opus 4.8 $5.5/$27.5, Sonnet 4.6 $3.3/$16.5 per M): median full review $4.82 uncached (finders $3.44, verifier-agentic $0.53, overlap judge $0.13, decide $0); p90 $10.83; pre-2026-08-12 with caching $2.18. Prompt caching has been 0% since 08-12 (mixed Bedrock+Anthropic chain → prompt_cache_style none) — filed as bug paternal-repayable-flamingo. $200 ≈ 40 full reviews uncached / ~90 cached, ~375 Pass-2-only re-runs, ~2,000 single-criterion single-turn calls, unlimited Pass-3 replays. usage.jsonl rows carry no ticket id (runner reads ticket_id, producers write ticket_ids) — child bug undamaged-adept-xenarthra.

Prior art honoured: ADR 0054 (field corpus is the instrument) and epic pastoral-aquatic-viper's rejection of live A/B batches; existing harnesses under docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/harnesses/ and docs/calibration/ are the starting point for corpus.py and tier0.py.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

Every change to the plan-review gate — a Pass-1 criterion prompt, a Pass-2 impact/validity question, a Pass-3 formula or threshold — lands on a handful of live dogfood reviews. No standing instrument answers "did this change make the gate better or worse?" before it ships; the prior calibration epic (`pastoral-aquatic-viper`, 6982) rejected live A/B batches on cost and parked the human gold set. The work is scattered across six epics and several orphan stories (`jira-reb-529`, `jira-reb-1589`, `fort-wisp-wren`, `spin-cub-usher`, `ridiculous-expert-mouse`, `auspicious-torrid-curlew`). This epic unifies them behind one harness.

The instrument already mostly exists as data. The live rebar store holds ~4,300 `plan_review_result_v2` sidecars on ~1,280 tickets (2026-06-27 → now; ~2,000 older ones pruned from the tree but recoverable from `origin/tickets` history) and `~/legacy-modernization-navigator` holds 74 more. Each v2 sidecar retains the raw Pass-1 findings (prose + evidence + scenarios + criteria), the complete Pass-2 answer vector (graded binaries + severity attributes), and the Pass-3 outputs (validity, impact, priority, the exact `block_threshold`, decision). The reviewed plan text is not stored but is reconstructable from ticket `EDIT`/`SNAPSHOT` history and verifiable byte-exactly against the stored `material_fingerprint`. The store also carries free outcome labels: 2,483 revise→re-review pairs (finding survival via `norm_id`), 208 verdict flips on byte-identical material (the reviewer-noise floor), 84 `plan_defect` bug closes, 89 `caused_by` links, 199 plan-PASS→completion-FAIL tickets, 18 reopens.

## Approach

Three eval tiers, ordered by cost, each measuring one pass in isolation while holding the others fixed:

- **Tier 0 — Pass-3 replay (zero LLM).** Re-run `review_kernel.decide.pass3_decide` (and the post-verdict floors) over the whole corpus with a candidate formula/threshold/routing overlay; diff against stored decisions. Generalises `docs/calibration/plan_v5_rescore.py` and `docs/experiments/calibrate_plan_review_thresholds.py`. Runs on every proposal, unlimited.
- **Tier 1 — Pass-2 replay (Sonnet, ~$0.5/review uncached).** Re-run the verifier with candidate questions/prompt on the *stored* Pass-1 findings plus reconstructed plan text via the `verify_findings(run_chunk=…)` seam; score per-question agreement against stored answers, then feed Tier 0.
- **Tier 2 — Pass-1 replay (Opus, ~$3.4/review uncached, plus a Tier-1 run on the new findings).** Re-run finders with candidate criteria on a fixed stratified sample (~20 tickets); compare finding sets by `norm_id`/criterion; single-criterion mode (~$0.17/call) for per-criterion edits.

Non-negotiable invariants, enforced by the harness rather than by convention:

1. **Hard budget.** A committed ledger tracks every eval call priced via `genai-prices`; every run pre-flights a cost estimate and refuses to start if projected spend would exceed the remaining allocation. Epic-wide cap is **$200** total with a $30 reserve; commissioning spend is planned at ≤$120 (one Tier-1 reproduction run to measure verifier noise, one Tier-2 baseline sample). Per-proposal costs are published.
2. **Model parity.** Every LLM re-run uses the exact production model class for that pass (frontier Opus for Pass 1, standard Sonnet for Pass 2) through **Bedrock only**, on a homogeneous provider chain (the mixed Bedrock+Anthropic fallback silently disables prompt caching and roughly doubles cost). The harness records the per-pass model id in every result, refuses to diff runs whose per-pass model ids differ, and refuses to start when the configured model differs from the corpus baseline's `provider_provenance.ran_model`. Substituting a cheaper model to save budget is forbidden: it confounds the measurement.
3. **Offline first.** Tier 0 and all label joins are pure functions of the frozen corpus; no proposal may be assessed on a live-only signal. Consistent with ADR 0054 (the field corpus is the instrument) and with 6982's rejection of live A/B.
4. **Noise-aware acceptance.** A change is reported as regressing/improving only when its label-proxy deltas exceed the noise band measured from identical-material flips and the Tier-1 reproduction run; otherwise "indistinguishable".

## Scope

New package `src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/` (corpus, labels, tier runners, ledger, report) with a `python -m rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay` entry; frozen corpus manifest + ledger + reports under `docs/experiments/plan-review-gate/replay/`; an ADR and a contributor guide section; fixes to `usage_log` ticket attribution. No CI provider dependency — everything runs locally.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A frozen, versioned replay corpus exists covering both stores (tree + git-recovered sidecars), with at-review plan text reconstructed and fingerprint-verified for ≥95% of v2 sidecars; verified by the corpus manifest's coverage counts.
- [ ] Outcome labels and a reviewer-noise floor are computed from the corpus with no LLM calls and joined to every review/finding; verified by a labels report listing counts per label source.
- [ ] A Pass-3 change (formula, threshold, routing overlay) can be assessed over the entire corpus with zero LLM calls, producing a diff report (verdict flips, per-criterion deltas, label-proxy precision/recall, friction rate); verified by replaying current code against itself with zero diffs and replaying a known historical threshold change reproducing its documented effect.
- [ ] A Pass-2 change can be assessed on a stratified sample using stored Pass-1 findings, with per-question agreement vs stored answers and downstream Tier-0 metrics; verified by a reproduction run (unchanged questions) whose agreement establishes the noise floor.
- [ ] A Pass-1 change can be assessed on a fixed stratified sample with finding-set comparison by `norm_id`/criterion and downstream Tier-1/Tier-0 metrics; verified by one baseline sample run.
- [ ] Every LLM eval call is priced and written to a committed ledger; a run whose pre-flight estimate exceeds remaining allocation is refused; total ledger spend at epic close is ≤ $200; verified by the ledger file and a test of the refusal path.
- [ ] Every eval result records the per-pass model id; the harness refuses to diff results with differing model ids and refuses to run a pass on a model other than its production class via Bedrock; verified by unit tests and by the ledger showing only Bedrock Opus/Sonnet ids.
- [ ] Prompt caching is confirmed active for eval runs (cache_read_tokens > 0 on the second call of a run); verified from the usage log.
- [ ] A contributor-facing protocol (ADR + docs) states which tier a proposal needs, the required report artifact, and the noise-band acceptance rule; verified by the docs landing and being referenced from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Child decomposition

Corpus builder (criterion 1) → outcome labels + noise floor (2) → Tier-0 harness (3) → Tier-1 harness (4) → Tier-2 harness (5) → budget ledger + model-parity guard + homogeneous Bedrock chain (6, 7, 8; includes the usage-log ticket-attribution bug) → change protocol ADR + docs (9). Folded-in existing work: `ridiculous-expert-mouse` (per-criterion fixture eval, a Tier-2 single-criterion consumer), `auspicious-torrid-curlew` (deterministic-floor candidates mined via Tier-0 replay), `brutal-idiocratic-rodent` (optional human-adjudicated gold subset, deferred enrichment). `jira-reb-529` is superseded: its recorded-LLM-response mocking is infeasible because prompts/responses are never persisted; the sidecar-replay tiers deliver its intent. `jira-reb-1589` and `fort-wisp-wren` are consumers that depend on this harness; `spin-cub-usher` and `yip-gem-teak` are related but out of scope.

## Non-goals

Changing any production criterion, question, or threshold (this epic builds the instrument); a full human-adjudicated gold set; live A/B in the production gate.
compiled_state.title: Plan-review process regression harness: replayable corpus + tiered evals under a hard $200 Bedrock budget
